policies.title: El Salvador: CA-4 ordinary-passport entry
policies.summary: DGME expressly permits Guatemalan, Honduran and Nicaraguan citizens to enter on a valid national identity document or passport. This records the ordinary-passport baseline as visa-free.
conditions: DGME permits a valid national identity document or passport; this policy records the ordinary-passport baseline only.
A foreign traveller already in the CA-4 region must hold a passport and remaining regional stay time granted on first entry.
Residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and special-document rules are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: current named Category A ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current RREE table and DGME’s linked full country list expressly assign these ordinary passports Category A, meaning visa-exempt.
conditions: The DGME list uses Category A for visa exemption; country-specific notes in the table are applied where they expressly change El Salvador’s ordinary-passport category.
Australian ordinary passports require a tourist card. That entry form/card is not treated as a visa or ETA.
The table’s non-El-Salvador CA-4 notes, and rules for diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless or special documents, are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: Ecuador ordinary passports — country-specific Category A
policies.summary: DGME’s full current list gives Ecuador a country-specific El Salvador instruction of Category A for all passports, despite the row’s general Category B label.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport baseline from the explicit El Salvador-specific note in the current DGME list.
Diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, transit, crew and special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: current named Category B/C ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current RREE table and DGME’s linked full country list place these ordinary passports in Category B (consular) or Category C (consulted), both of which require advance visa authorization.
conditions: Category B is consular/sin consulta and Category C is consulted; both are advance-visa categories under RREE’s current definitions.

DGME’s online PEI is available to Category B/C applicants, but applicants may also apply at a diplomatic mission; an approved PEI is stamped in the passport at entry. It is therefore not a nationality-wide eVisa classification.
The RREE selector can depend on a valid United States, Canadian or Schengen visa and legal residence. Those third-country-document conditions are not nationality-wide classifications.

Visa grant, duration, entries, fee, sponsoring evidence, port and admission/security controls remain case- or route-specific; residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: Taiwan ordinary passports — country-specific Category C
policies.summary: DGME’s full current list gives the China (Taiwan) row a country-specific El Salvador instruction of Category C, despite the row’s general Category A label.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport baseline from the explicit El Salvador-specific note in the current DGME list.
Category C is a consulted advance visa; diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, transit, crew and special-document cases are excluded.

conflicts.explanation: DGME’s current full list assigns Bolivian ordinary passports Category B (consular/sin consulta), an advance-visa route rather than visa-free entry.
DGME’s current full list assigns Pakistani ordinary passports Category C (consulted). PEI is advance authorization later stamped at entry and is not a nationality-wide eVisa.
